title: Arctic Wildlife Research Suffers as Geopolitical Competition Grows
summary: As national security and the hunt for rare minerals come to dominate Arctic agendas, governments are slashing support for wildlife research. Scientists say the loss of monitoring is unprecedented and comes as climate change dramatically reshapes life in the Far North.

Decades ago, one of the world’s largest subpopulations of nesting eider ducks spent its summers on tiny Mitivik Island, near the mouth of Hudson Bay. But as concern grew, in the 1990s, over their steep decline globally, the Canadian government set up a rudimentary research station near the island in the hopes of forestalling a collapse.
summary_zh: 隨著國家安全和尋找稀有礦物成為北極議程的主導，各國政府正在削減對野生動物研究的支持。科學家表示，監測的喪失是前所未有的，氣候變遷極大地重塑了遠北地區的生活。
幾十年前，世界上最大的築巢絨鴨亞群之一在哈德遜灣入海口附近的米蒂維克小島上度過了夏天。但隨著人們對 20 世紀 90 年代全球經濟急劇衰退的擔憂日益加劇，加拿大政府在島上附近設立了一個簡陋的研究站，希望能防止經濟崩潰。
